test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 27 Oct 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper mixed two kinds of rice in the ratio 1 : 5. Type 1 rice costs Rs. 65 per kg and type 2 rice costs Rs. 95 per kg. He sold the mixed rice at Rs. 99 per kg. Find his gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weighted average CP = (1 × 65 + 5 × 95) ÷ (1 + 5)

CP = (65 + 475) ÷ 6 = 540 ÷ 6 = Rs. 90/kg

SP = Rs. 99/kg

Profit % = [(99 − 90) ÷ 90] × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Type 1 to Type 2 = 1 : 5

Cost of Type 1 (CP₁) = Rs. 65/kg

Cost of Type 2 (CP₂) = Rs. 95/kg

Selling Price of Mixture (SP) = Rs. 99/kg

**Formula Used:**

Mean CP = (n₁ × CP₁ + n₂ × CP₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

Gain % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 Alligation Method (Finding Mean CP)
 
 CP1: 65
 
 CP2: 95
 
 Mean CP
 
• 
 
•

• 
 Ratio: 1
 Ratio: 5
 Gain = SP - CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let weights be 1 kg and 5 kg respectively.

⇒ Total Cost Price = (1 × 65) + (5 × 95)

⇒ Total CP = 65 + 475 = Rs. 540

⇒ Total Weight = 1 + 5 = 6 kg

⇒ Mean CP per kg = 540 ÷ 6 = Rs. 90

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 99

⇒ Gain = 99 − 90 = Rs. 9

⇒ Gain % = (9 ÷ 90) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 10% (equivalent to 0.1 in decimal format)

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

Ratio of quantities = (Higher price − Mean price) : (Mean price − Lower price).

Gain and Loss Percentage

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Calculations are always based on CP unless specified.

Mixture Price Formula

The weighted average price is Pₘ = (w₁P₁ + w₂P₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂), where w is weight and P is price.</p
